intendedAudience: Promoters, directors, and legal officers of established retail houses, jewellery chains, textile emporiums, and manufacturing firms in Thrissur holding aging trademarks.
quickAnswer: A registered trademark in India remains valid for 10 years from the original application date under Section 25 of the Trade Marks Act 1999. In Thrissur, established brands can file Form TM-R for renewal within one year prior to expiration at the statutory fee of ₹9,000 per class (note: no MSME discounts apply to renewals). If missed, renewal is permissible with a late surcharge within six months post-expiry. Beyond that, a one-year restoration window applies under Section 25(4). Allowing a mark to lapse destroys statutory presumption of ownership, exposing multi-decade enterprise goodwill to competitors.

h2Sections.h2: The 10-Year Renewal Lifecycle: Preserving Multi-Generational Goodwill
content: Thrissur is home to some of Kerala's most enduring commercial enterprises. Heritage gold retail houses, multi-decade textile emporiums, pioneering publishing presses, and pharmaceutical laboratories have built generational equity under their commercial brand names. Many of these established brands secured trademark registrations under the Trade Marks Act 1999 during the early digital filing era.

However, trademark rights are not permanent without active statutory maintenance. Under Section 25 of the Act, a trademark registration expires exactly 10 years from the date of initial filing. If an enterprise neglects to file a timely renewal application, the Trade Marks Registry removes the mark from the Register, instantly extinguishing the owner's statutory monopoly and allowing opportunistic competitors to claim the abandoned name.
The Trade Marks Rules 2017 define three distinct procedural windows governing trademark renewal, managed under the jurisdiction of the Trade Marks Registry Chennai:
1. Standard Renewal Window (1 Year Before Expiry): Form TM-R can be submitted at any time within 12 months preceding the expiration date. The official statutory fee is ₹9,000 per class for e-filing.

2. Late Renewal Window with Surcharge (Up to 6 Months After Expiry): If the expiration date passes, the applicant has a 6-month grace period to file Form TM-R accompanied by a statutory surcharge of ₹4,500 (total ₹13,500 per class).

3. Restoration Window (6 Months to 1 Year After Expiry): If the mark is officially removed from the Register for non-renewal, the proprietor can file for Restoration and Renewal under Section 25(4) within one year from expiration, paying ₹18,000 per class and submitting a formal statement explaining the failure to renew.

h2Sections.h2: Critical Legal Distinction: No MSME Concessions on Renewals
content: A frequent surprise for Thrissur business owners is discovering that the 50% MSME statutory fee concession granted on initial Form TM-A filings does not apply to trademark renewals.

Under the First Schedule of the Trade Marks Rules 2017, the statutory fee for filing Form TM-R is fixed uniformly at ₹9,000 per class for all categories of applicants—including individuals, micro enterprises, and large public corporations. Planning adequate legal budget across multi-class portfolios is therefore essential for established retail chains holding registrations across Classes 14, 25, 35, and 43.

callout.title: The Catastrophic Cost of Trademark Lapse
callout.text: If a trademark lapses completely past the one-year restoration deadline, you forfeit your statutory right to file an infringement lawsuit under Section 29. A competitor can apply for your exact brand name, forcing you into expensive, multi-year passing-off litigation.

h2Sections.h2: Pre-Renewal Legal Audit Checklist for Thrissur Brands
content: Before submitting Form TM-R, conduct this comprehensive intellectual property audit across your enterprise assets:
checklist: Verify the exact expiration date and class numbers on your official Certificate of Registration
Confirm whether the registered proprietor entity name or commercial address has changed (file Form TM-M if updates are needed)
Check whether the registered logo design has undergone modern graphic alterations requiring a fresh TM-A filing
Submit Form TM-R through the IP India e-filing portal and obtain the official digital filing acknowledgment
Track the Registry status until the Renewal Certificate is officially generated and the next 10-year validity is recorded
Ensure ongoing commercial sales invoices display the registered ® symbol alongside the updated mark

h2Sections.h2: Frequently Asked Questions About Trademark Renewal
content:
Q: Does the Trade Marks Registry send a reminder before a trademark expires?
Under Section 25(3), the Registrar is legally required to send a formal notice (Form RG-3) to the registered proprietor at their recorded address of service before removing the mark. However, relying on this notice is dangerous, as postal notices are frequently misdelivered or sent to outdated addresses. The registered owner bears ultimate responsibility for tracking renewal deadlines.

Q: Can I update our company's registered office address at the time of renewal?
Address updates cannot be made directly on Form TM-R. You must file Form TM-M with the prescribed fee (₹900) to officially record the change of address in the Register of Trade Marks.

Q: What happens if our trademark registration is held in the name of a deceased partner?
Before filing the renewal, you must file a transmission or assignment petition on Form TM-P to formally record the legal heirs or reconstituted partnership as the new registered proprietors.

faqs.question: How long is a trademark valid in India before it must be renewed?
faqs.answer: A trademark registration is valid for exactly 10 years from the original application date and can be renewed indefinitely every 10 years by filing Form TM-R.

faqs.question: Is there an MSME discount for trademark renewal fees in India?
faqs.answer: No. Unlike initial trademark applications, the Trade Marks Rules 2017 do not provide MSME fee concessions on Form TM-R renewals. The fee is uniformly ₹9,000 per class.

faqs.question: Can a lapsed trademark be restored after its 10-year expiration?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 25(4) of the Trade Marks Act, a removed mark can be restored and renewed by filing Form TM-R with the restoration fee within one year from the expiration date.
